benchmarks: SEC-Bench, PatchEval (Python, Go, JavaScript), Multi-SWE-bench (C++ subset)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Cognitive Deficiency' (S1): feedback-driven repair loops without experiential memory treat failed-test feedback merely as a rejection signal, so agents 'oscillate between invalid solutions rather than generating a correct fix.' Mitigated by L3 Refinement-Trajectory Memory, which stores explicit failed-patch -> correction-delta -> transition-rule triples (Eq.5) from prior 'failure-to-success' trajectories and is activated specifically after a failed verification cycle to guide the next Patcher iteration (S3.4 Phase2). RQ2 ablation confirms L3 is the single most significant individual contributor to repair success.
cita: Liu et al. (2026). MemRepair: Hierarchical Memory for Agentic Repository-Level Vulnerability Repair.
notes: S3.3 three-tier hierarchy: L1 History-Fix (mined offline from CVEFixes, 14,063 entries, EPISODICA project-specific past fixes), L2 Security-Pattern (successful repair instance + natural-language Rationale = generalized defensive pattern, PROCEDIMENTAL), L3 Refinement-Trajectory (failed patch + correction delta + transition rule, collected in real-time during repair). S3.3.4 retrieval: two-tier priority P1(intra-project, same CWE+lang)->P2(cross-project generalization) via text-embedding-3-small cosine similarity (EMBEDDINGS) with explicit ranking/filtering (RANKING); temporal constraint excludes future entries (leakage prevention). S3.3.3: 'lightweight management strategies: (1) deduplication (cosine similarity>0.95 merged, CONSOLIDACION) and (2) recency-weighted pruning (entries unretrieved over a window periodically removed, OLVIDO).' 'Collaborative multi-agent system' explicitly named: Locator/Patcher/Verifier agents (S2/S3.2) all draw on the shared L1/L2/L3 hierarchy -> multiagente=SI. Verifier gates writes: success updates L2, failure->success transition updates L3 (ADMISION). Results: 58.0% SEC-Bench, 58.2% PatchEval, 30.58%/30.6% Multi-SWE-bench(C++), beating InfCode-C++ (25.60%) by 19% (matches abstract); Cost = avg USD/task explicitly reported (S4.3) -> COSTO-TOKENS; Location Accuracy = OTRA. RQ2 (S979-1119) explicit ablation isolating L1/L2/L3 individually, Table3 -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. NEGATIVO sense(a): L3 explicitly stores FAILURE states (P_fail) as first-class memory content. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds CONSOLIDACION, MULTIAGENTE, PROCEDIMENTAL, WRITE found in full text.

benchmarks: MemFail (own): Conditional-Facts (Easy/Hard), Coexisting-Facts, Persona-Retrieval, Long-Hop; systems evaluated: Mem0, A-MEM, SimpleMem, StructMem
fallos_mitigaciones: Diagnostic taxonomy, no mitigation proposed/tested (only future directions sketched): Summary failure (summarization strips qualifying conditions/severity, e.g. 'deathly allergic' -> 'allergic', S3.2); Storage failure (refuses to overwrite outdated facts on contradiction, OR incorrectly rejects valid coexisting facts as contradictory, e.g. treating 'likes pizza'+'likes ramen' as conflicting); Retrieval failure (fails to return relevant memories, or returns semantically-similar-but-contextually-wrong ones). S6: 'no single system dominates: graph-based StructMem excels at causal reasoning but collapses on coexisting-fact retrieval, Mem0 shows the opposite pattern'; scaling retrieval depth k or model strength yields little/negative improvement -> systems 'bound by architectural constraints.' Two UNEXPLORED future directions proposed (not implemented/tested): mixture-of-experts memory architectures and task-adaptive token scaling.
cita: Garg et al. (2026). MemFail: Stress-Testing Failure Modes of LLM Memory Systems.
notes: Pure diagnostic benchmark (S3.1): formalizes ANY memory system as Summarize->Store->Retrieve and isolates failure at each operation across 4 tested systems -> mem_tipos/representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA for MemFail itself (it MEASURES others' mechanisms, Table1 shows each tested system's own S/S/R implementation). S5.1-5.2 evaluation loop grades each of N required memories into storage-check/summary-check/retrieval-check/reasoning-check per query (mide_lectura=SI, isolates read-side failures specifically -> RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO in F); 'faithful storage that preserves the semantics of the original experience' + storage failure = 'refusing to overwrite outdated facts' is a direct staleness/fidelity axis -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. Q1/Q2/Q3 (S6) systematically sweep retrieval depth k, test-taker model strength, and token consumption (Fig1-3) -> treated as ABLATION-style controlled sweeps; Table2 measured statistics report avg tokens/entry (cl100k_base) -> COSTO-TOKENS. Human validation: gpt-5-mini judge 98% accurate / 98.4% correct error-type classification on 100 hand-graded examples. NEGATIVO sense(b): 'current systems are bound by architectural constraints rather than model intelligence or context budget' -- systematic negative finding across all 4 evaluated systems. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds FIDELIDAD (faithful-storage axis) and COSTO (token-consumption tradeoff analysis).

benchmarks: ExpSuite (ExpSuite-Static: ARC-C, CommonsenseQA, GPQA, MMLU, OBQA, GSM8K, GSM-Symbolic, MATH, HumanEval+, MBPP+; ExpSuite-Agentic: ALFWorld, AppWorld)
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Surface relevance is not the same as experience utility' (S1): flat nearest-neighbor retrieval selects semantically-similar experiences that provide little downstream benefit, while a truly useful (transferable-strategy) experience may not be among the nearest neighbors. Mitigated by (i) graph diffusion beyond flat kNN (personalized PageRank expansion from semantic seeds, S3.3) and (ii) a trainable retrieval copilot with utility-aware ranking (UCB score combining estimated utility u_v + exploration bonus, Eq.8-9) optimized via PPO on a reward directly comparing executor performance WITH vs WITHOUT retrieved experience (Eq.14, S3.4) -- so retrieval learns to favor experiences that are empirically beneficial, not just topically similar.
cita: Feng et al. (2026). ExpGraph: Model-Agnostic Experience Learning with Graph-Structured Memory for LLM Agents.
notes: S3.2 Experience Graph G=(V,E): trajectories tau=(x,xi,y,s) summarized into node v=(e_v,h_v,u_v,n_v) (text + embedding + online utility + retrieval count); high-scoring trajectories -> 'skills' (PROCEDIMENTAL), low-scoring -> 'lessons/failure modes' (EPISODICA); nodes connected to top-K cosine-similar neighbors, theta threshold (Eq.3) -> representacion=HIBRIDA (vector+graph). S3.3 retrieval: (a) semantic seeding by cosine similarity (EMBEDDINGS), (b) personalized-PageRank graph diffusion with copilot-controlled restart prob rho (GRAFO), (c) UCB utility-aware ranking mixing similarity+utility-confidence via copilot-controlled lambda (RANKING). S3.4: new candidate node filtered for near-duplicates before insertion (ADMISION); node utility/count updated online each retrieval event u_v<-(1-beta)u_v+beta*r (ACTUALIZACION); 'when the graph exceeds its capacity budget, nodes with low utility and low retrieval frequency are evicted' (OLVIDO+PRESUPUESTO trigger). Reward r=(s_with-s_without)+eta*s_with (Eq.14) IS a direct read-utility measurement -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. Table2/3: ExpGraph beats strongest baseline by 12.2%/4.7% (static, small/large executor) and 21.4%/12.7% (agentic), reducing avg interaction steps 12.7%/21.6% (matches abstract) -> ITERACION. Ablation studies (S4/App G.3) isolate graph-structure, utility-ranking, adaptive-retrieval contributions. NEGATIVO sense(a): low-scoring trajectories explicitly distilled into 'lessons, such as failure modes, invalid actions, or constraints to avoid' -- stored as first-class negative content. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds PROCEDIMENTAL, WRITE.

benchmarks: CL-Bench (own): Codebase Adaptation, Database Exploration, Blind Spectrum Monitoring, Cohort Studies, Exploitable Poker, Sales Prediction; systems evaluated: Full-context ICL, ICL Notepad, Mem0, ACE, Claude Code, Codex
fallos_mitigaciones: Core finding, no fix proposed by this diagnostic benchmark (only measured): 'agents frequently overfit to immediate observations or fail to reuse knowledge across instances, and dedicated memory systems do not fix this -- naive ICL outperforms systems dedicated to memory management' (abstract). Concretely, the running Database Exploration example (Fig.1) shows agents that are 'rigid in early, incorrect beliefs' and, after a database migration invalidates part of past experience, 'blindly reusing past experience -> FAILURE' (query against a renamed table errors out) unless the system detects and discards the stale experience. ACE (an explicit consolidation/playbook mechanism) ranks 9th/12 by gain while incurring the HIGHEST cost of any evaluated system ($62.8/run, Table1) -- a dedicated memory mechanism underperforming plain full-context ICL at higher cost.
cita: Asawa et al. (2026). Continual Learning Bench: Evaluating Frontier AI Systems in Real-World Stateful Environments.
notes: Pure benchmark (no own memory mechanism; evaluates ICL/ICL-Notepad/Mem0/ACE/Claude-Code/Codex as 'systems') -> mem_tipos/representacion/operaciones/trigger/retrieval=NA. S3.2-3.3: 6 expert-validated domains each with 'shared latent structure' (codebase layout, DB schema, opponent strategies) a stateful system must discover online; 2 tasks (Codebase Adaptation, Database Exploration) explicitly include CONCEPT DRIFT (a database migration mid-schedule) requiring detection+discarding of stale past experience -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI (staleness handling is a core design axis, Fig.1). S4.1-4.2: 'gain' metric g_t = r_t^sf - r_t^sl explicitly isolates the causal contribution of accumulated state/memory vs a stateless rerun of the SAME system on the SAME instance -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (this IS a read-utility measurement, at the whole-system level). Table1: full-context ICL+Sonnet4.6 ranks #1 by both normalized reward (22.3%) and gain (25.4%); Cost reports mean USD/rollout per system (COSTO-TOKENS) alongside normalized reward/gain (EXITO) and the bespoke gain metric itself (OTRA). NEGATIVO sense(b): headline result IS that dedicated memory systems underperform naive full-context ICL -- systematic negative evidence about current memory-management mechanisms. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO) + adds RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO (gain metric), FIDELIDAD (concept-drift/staleness design), COSTO (explicit $/rollout table).

benchmarks: own constructed diagnostic harness (running-total computation + budget-approval agent + access-control agent); tested against mem0, LangMem, and a verbatim VectorStoreRetrieverMemory control
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Manufactured confidence': fact-extraction consolidation (mem0, LangMem) rewrites a casual, hedged remark into a confident, dated assertion that later agent steps obey like a verified fact. TWO sources: (1) natural staleness -- a once-true hedge goes stale and its correction is never stored (no attacker needed), producing confident-wrong grants on 0.69 (mem0)/0.75 (LangMem) of requests (Table3); (2) adversarial injection -- one planted sentence is laundered into an authoritative dated fact by BOTH real products (100% laundering rate) vs 0% on the verbatim control (Table7), yielding 0.72 unauthorized-grant with no defense (Table6). 'The obvious fixes fail': a passive 'unverified' tag is leaky and provider-dependent (0.00-0.81, Table5/6); an active 'do not trust this' instruction (distrust) stops the cascade everywhere (0.00 wrong-decision) but by ABDICATION not discrimination -- it escalates 100% of requests even on CORRECT memory (Table8). The fix that actually works: preserve tentative phrasing AT THE STORE (do not de-hedge; hygiene, not an adversarial defense) PLUS add a redundant/second source (authoritative directory) to verify against, which restores correct discrimination (wrong-grant 0.00, zero escalation, Table2) even under an assertive poisoned memory.
cita: Kwon (2026). Manufactured Confidence: How Memory Consolidation Turns Hearsay into Confident Facts.
notes: S1/Fig1: memory products (mem0, LangMem) extract conversation into stored 'facts' retrieved by later steps -> representacion=DOCS-ARCHIVOS (extracted text facts), retrieval=EMBEDDINGS (paper explicitly probes the underlying BGE-small vector: hedge IS linearly recoverable there, balanced accuracy 1.00, so the loss happens at the LLM-rewrite/consolidation step, not the embedding -- CONSOLIDACION is the operation under study, title-level). S3 cross of 7 framings (bare/attributed/forged-authority all confident vs 4 hedge types) isolates that the agent obeys CONFIDENCE not SOURCE (Table1: confident framings grant 0.81 regardless of attribution/forged 'system of record'; hedges collapse grants near 0.00). Table3: with an in-context correction present, memory reconciles/downgrades (ACTUALIZACION, grants 0/16); without one, staleness persists (grants 0.69-0.75) -- direct fidelidad_procedencia=SI evidence (this IS the paper's core axis: staleness + provenance-blindness). Table2: redundant authoritative-directory source restores discrimination (wrong-grant 0.00). 5 models tested (Claude Sonnet/Haiku, Llama-70B, GPT-4o-mini, Qwen-72B), all deterministic at temp=0 -- systematic controlled manipulation of framing/defense/source = ABLATION per calibration vara E (not a standard task BENCHMARK-E2E). handoff=CONTENIDO: 'LLM agents carry conclusions across steps AND SESSIONS in compressed memory' -- the manufactured-confident fact IS the content that travels. NEGATIVO sense(b) + SEGURIDAD (cs.CR; explicit memory-poisoning/injection attack, 'PoisonedRAG corrupts what is retrieved; we study a memory-store variant that corrupts what is recorded'). F confirms F_screening (FIDELIDAD;NEGATIVO) + adds CONSOLIDACION, SEGURIDAD, WRITE.

benchmarks: own paper-section Manim-animation dataset (memory-building 39 tasks / fixed-probe 33 / cross-test 40); baselines: Manim-code RAG, Random EMB, VLM-reflection-only
fallos_mitigaciones: 'Cross-task forgetting' (S1, Fig.1): a reflection pipeline closes the INTRA-task loop (observe error, revise, retry) but every lesson paid for in tokens is thrown away before the next task starts, so a structurally similar future task repeats the same layout/formula mistake and pays the full reflection cost again. Mitigated by the dual-channel Episodic Memory Bank: positive channel M+ = soft Reference Examples (success rationale, write-gated at score>=85), negative channel M- = hard Known Pitfalls (validated failure->success transitions, causal-attribution gated, requires score delta>=5 for visual transitions) injected into the Coder prompt on retrieval. Table1/Fig3: EMB@200 improves blind-human Pass@1 to 84.9% (vs 68.5% VLM-reflection-only, 69.6% Random-EMB, and even 83.3% for a strong matched-budget static Manim-code RAG baseline) while cutting reflection rounds to 6.5 (vs 12.2 baseline).
cita: Jiang et al. (2026). ManimAgent: Self-Evolving Multimodal Agents for Visual Education.
notes: S3.1-3.3: dual-channel Episodic Memory Bank M=M+ union M-, backed by 1 SQLite table + 2 per-polarity Faiss IndexFlatIP vector indices (representacion=HIBRIDA); M+ records a success rationale (soft prior, PROCEDIMENTAL template) per high-scoring scene (u*>=theta_high=85, ADMISION); M- records a structured 'validated failure pattern' (EPISODICA, causal-attribution-gated: crash->success text transitions accepted unconditionally, visual transitions require delta_fail>=5 score-margin, ADMISION) via LLM-distilled lessons (NOT literal diffs -- explicit CONSOLIDACION step). Retrieval by task-embedding cosine similarity (all-MiniLM-L6-v2, EMBEDDINGS), disjoint per-polarity indices (a query on M+ never returns M- records). Explicit six named agents (Storyboarder, Coder, text Reviewer, VLM Reviewer, Visual Reviser, Lesson Distiller/Rationale Writer) sharing the single EMB -> multiagente=SI (paper self-describes as 'self-evolving multi-agent system'). S3.3 'Provenance, deduplication, and embedder pinning': provenance block (run id, scene id, extraction source, transition ordinal, before/after scores) for write-time dedup; embedder identity PINNED at first creation, 'refused on reopen if a different encoder is requested' preventing silent re-embedding drift between writes/reads -> fidelidad_procedencia=SI. 'No capacity, no eviction... grow monotonically' -- explicitly NO OLVIDO mechanism. Table1 ablations (channel isolation No-M+/No-M-/No-memory, gate stringency, Top-1 retrieval depth, Weak-VLM reviewer) directly measure read-side utility -> mide_lectura=SI/RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO. NEGATIVO sense(a): M- is explicitly a negative/failure channel storing 'Known Pitfalls' (validated failures) as first-class memory content. F confirms F_screening (NEGATIVO;RETRIEVAL-MEDIDO) + adds CONSOLIDACION (LLM-distilled lessons), FIDELIDAD (provenance/embedder-pinning), MULTIAGENTE, WRITE.
